'''Isiah Manuel Warner''' (born July 20, 1946) is the Boyd and Phillip W. West Professor of Surface and Analytical Chemistry and the Vice President for Strategic Initiatives at [[Louisiana State University]]. He’s also a professor at the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]]. Warner has won numerous national and international awards for chemistry and mentoring of students<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.avoyellestoday.com/news/dr-isiah-warner-receives-national-award-mentorship|title=Dr. Isiah Warner receives national award for mentorship|date=2019-02-08|website=Avoyelles Today|language=en|access-date=2020-01-21}}</ref> in the sciences. He has published over 350 refereed publications and has several patents.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Pitre|first=Emile|date=2019-12-23|title=Isiah Warner (1946- )|url=https://www.blackpast.org/african-american-history/isiah-warner-1946/|access-date=2020-08-16|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Biography==
Isiah Warner was born in [[Bunkie, Louisiana]] in 1946. He is a graduate of [[Southern University]] where he received his BS degree in chemistry.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.lsu.edu/osi/about/meet-warner.php|title=Meet Vice President Isiah M. Warner {{!}} LSU Office of Strategic Initiatives|website=www.lsu.edu|access-date=2020-01-21}}</ref> Warner received his doctorate in Analytical Chemistry from the [[University of Washington]] in 1977.<ref name=":0" /> Following a post-doctoral research experience, Warner started his academic career at [[Texas A&M University]] where he was the first African American Chemistry faculty, and where received tenure and promotion to associate professor.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/isiah-m-warner-40|title=Isiah M. Warner's Biography|website=The HistoryMakers|language=en|access-date=2020-01-21}}</ref> Following receipt of tenure and promotion, Warner moved his research laboratory to [[Emory University]] and was promoted to full professor in 1986. In 1992, Warner returned to Louisiana and serves as the Phillip W. West Professor of Surface and Analytical Chemistry at Louisiana State University. He retired as Professor Emeritus in December 2021, with his most recent role being the Vice President of Strategic Initiatives at LSU and serves as a Howard Hughes Medical Institute Professor.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hhmi.org/science-education/programs/hhmi-professors-0#W|title=HHMI Professors {{!}} HHMI.org|website=www.hhmi.org|access-date=2020-02-11}}</ref>

Warner received an honorary doctorate from [[Marquette University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marquette.edu/university-honors/honorary-degrees/warner.php|title=Dr. Isiah M. Warner // University Honors // Marquette University|website=www.marquette.edu|access-date=2020-01-21}}</ref>  He has been recognized for his chemical research and mentoring.<ref>{{Citation|title=ACS Award for Encouraging Disadvantaged Students into Careers in the Chemical Sciences|date=2020-01-16|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ACS_Award_for_Encouraging_Disadvantaged_Students_into_Careers_in_the_Chemical_Sciences&oldid=936085756|work=Wikipedia|language=en|access-date=2020-01-21}}</ref> Warner was named a fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2009. He is a recipient of the NOBCChE [[Percy L. Julian Award]].<ref>{{Citation|title=Percy Lavon Julian|date=2020-01-19|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Percy_Lavon_Julian&oldid=936570349|work=Wikipedia|language=en|access-date=2020-01-21}}</ref>

== Research and Mentoring ==
Warner is an analytical/materials Chemist, with research focuses on [[fluorescence spectroscopy]], organized media, and [[ionic liquid]] chemistry, particularly as applied to solid phase materials.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Isiah M. Warner|url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/isiah-m-warner|access-date=2020-08-16|website=HHMI.org|language=en}}</ref> He is known for his mentoring of Chemistry students, and focus on the advancement of women and chemists of color. He has won numerous awards for his mentoring including. He has graduated 67 PhD students from his group, including a significant number of women and minorities, helping to make Louisiana State University the leader in producing women and African American PhD students.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Makings of a Master Mentor|url=https://lsuscienceblog.squarespace.com/blog/2019/8/26/the-makings-of-a-master-mentor|access-date=2020-08-16|website=Science Next|date=27 August 2019 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Warner was born in 1946 in DeQuincy, Louisiana to Humphrey and Erma Warner. His interest in science started young, when he conducted his first experiment by drinking kerosene to see why it created light.<ref name=":2" /> He and his wife, Della Blount Warner, have three children: Isiah Jr., Edward and Chideha.<ref name=":2" />
